land.text: the Ottoman vilayets of the Syrian interior, entered by the Arab forces on 1 October 1918; the page names the preceding entity as OETA East without a start date

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws part of this land (227 cells: Damascus, Amman, Deraa) inside its Kingdom of Hejaz shapes of 1918 and 1919; the kingdom-of-hejaz dossier removes it.

land.text: Damascus and Syria, which 'surrendered to French forces on 25 July 1920'; General Gouraud divided the French mandate territory into several smaller states on 1 September 1920

successors.note: A pro-French government under Aladdin Al-Droubi was installed the same day.

land.text: Transjordan, which became 'for a short time, a no man's land' after the Battle of Maysalun (July 1920) until Abdullah's Emirate of Transjordan of April 1921

successors.note: The Emirate of Transjordan page lists the Arab Kingdom of Syria among the Emirate's predecessors and says the page does not describe what territory the kingdom held in Transjordan.

rulers.name: Faisal (Emir)
rulers.title: Emir
rulers.note: Emir 5 October 1918 to 8 March 1920 (page reign table).

rulers.name: Faisal I
rulers.title: King
rulers.note: King 8 March 1920 to 28 July 1920 per the reign table (the text and infobox end the kingdom on 25 July 1920).

correction.text: Syria's interior and Transjordan north of Ma'an, a reading of the Damascus Program's limits without the French-held coast

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1918-1920: Cliopatria has no row for Faisal's Syria and draws its southern part (227 cells: Damascus, Deraa, Amman) inside the Kingdom of Hejaz shapes of 1918-1919. The page gives no area and no boundary except the Damascus Program of 2 July 1919 (the Taurus Range in the north, a line from Rafah to al-Jauf in the south, the Euphrates and Khabur and a line near Abu-Kamal in the east, the Mediterranean in the west), which is a programme, and a map of the state's 'greatest extent in January 1920'. The shape is Syria without its Mediterranean governorates (Latakia, Tartus, which the page does not give the kingdom) and northern Jordan without Ma'an and Aqaba (Hejazi); it is a reading of the Program at confidence 1-2 and 846 cells less the coast, far larger than Cliopatria's 227 cells.

ledger.note: 5 October 1918: Faisal announces an Arab government at Damascus. He announced 'a fully and absolutely independent Arab constitutional government' with Allenby's permission (the Arab Revolt page has the Arab troops riding into Damascus on 1 October 1918). The state's earlier entity is OETA East, undated on the page.

8 March 1920: the Emirate is proclaimed a kingdom with Faisal I as king and Hashim al-Atassi as prime minister. 'Proclaimed a kingdom on 8 March 1920' (the Damascus Program of 2 July 1919 had called for a constitutional monarchy under Faisal). Same state, same colour.

region.text: the road to Damascus and the city, where the French defeated the Syrian army

ledger.note: 24 July 1920: the French invade after the ultimatum of 14 July. General Gouraud 'gave an ultimatum to King Faisal on 14 July 1920'; at the Battle of Maysalun on 24 July 'the Syrian army was easily defeated by the French'. The page gives no site for the battle, so the zone is Damascus's approaches.
25 July 1920: the fighting ends with the surrender of Damascus to French forces.

region.text: Damascus and the Syrian interior; Transjordan becomes no man's land

ledger.note: 25 July 1920: Damascus falls and the kingdom ends. The kingdom 'surrendered to French forces on 25 July 1920' (the infobox gives the siege as 25 July and the reign table 28 July); Faisal was expelled in August 1920 and Gouraud divided the territory on 1 September 1920. Transjordan was left 'for a short time, a no man's land' (Transjordan page).

wars.name: Franco-Syrian War
wars.outcome: The French defeated the Syrian army at Maysalun on 24 July 1920 and took Damascus on 25 July; Faisal was expelled in August.
wars.note: Ultimatum of General Gouraud on 14 July 1920; the page's infobox and text differ on the siege date (24 or 25 July) and on the end (25 or 28 July).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line; the Damascus Program of July 1919 states claims, the Franco-Syrian frontier at the coast is not on the page.

sources.title: Arab Kingdom of Syria
sources.note: Announced 5 October 1918, kingdom 8 March 1920, ended 25 July 1920; the Damascus Program of 2 July 1919; no area.

sources.title: Emirate of Transjordan
sources.note: Opened for kingdom-of-hejaz; cited here for Transjordan as 'a no man's land' after Maysalun.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks, written as a direct counterpart of kingdom-of-hejaz (whose Cliopatria 1918-1919 shapes carried this land). One page opened for the dossier (Arab Kingdom of Syria; the Emirate of Transjordan page was opened for the Hejaz dossier). The extent is the weak part: the page gives only the Damascus Program's claims and a map (not described), so the shape is a reading of the Program less the coast, much larger than Cliopatria's 227 cells; a gap-filler should open OETA East / Occupied Enemy Territory Administration and Franco-Syrian War for the real administered zone (Aleppo, Homs, Hama are plausible but not on the page). Not recorded: the British withdrawal from OETA East on 26 November 1919 (the page calls it the point of independence as an emirate; no territorial change recorded), the Syrian National Congress's Damascus Program of 2 July 1919, and Faisal's expulsion in August 1920. The French mandate dossier (french-mandate-for-syria-and-lebanon, Cliopatria row from 1920) is the successor of the Syrian land; Transjordan is no man's land from July 1920 to 1921 (kingdom-of-jordan's early years). Ma'an and Aqaba are left to the Hejaz here and in kingdom-of-hejaz (annexed by Hussein in 1918), although the Transjordan page says Ma'an was held by OETA East and Faisal's Syria, while Hussein never accepted this: a disputed zone between the two dossiers in 1918-1920 for which no page gives a campaign, so no contest event is recorded. Wikidata is not on the page.
